# C++ break Statement

#### Course: Learn C++ Basics

## C++ break Statement

Sometimes, we may need to end a loop immediately in the middle. In such cases, the break statement is used.

The break statement terminates the loop immediately when it is encountered. Let's see an example of it.

```cpp
1#include <iostream>
2using namespace std;
3
4int main() {
5
6    for (int i = 1; i < 6; ++i) {
7        cout << i << endl;
8
9        break;
10
11    }
12
13    cout << "This is outside the loop.";
14
15    return 0;
16}
```

Output

```text
1
This is outside the loop.
```

Here, the loop should iterate 5 times from i equal to 1 to 5. However, after printing 1 (the value of i), the break statement is encountered and the loop terminates.

In most cases, we'll want to terminate the loop in the middle only when a specific condition is met. That's why the break statement is almost always used inside an if statement.

```cpp
1#include <iostream>
2using namespace std;
3
4int main() {
5
6    for (int i = 1; i < 6; ++i) {
7        cout << i << endl;
8
9
10        if (i == 3) {
11            break;
12        }
13
14    }
15
16    cout << "This is outside the loop.";
17
18    return 0;
19}
```

Output

```text
1
2
3
This is outside the loop.
```

Here's how the break statement works.
